channel.title: Hashbeam
channel.description: Hashbeam reports crypto news: protocol upgrades, network security, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation and market structure across blockchains and tokens.

item.title: Injective and BDACS plan KRW1 settlement for tokenized assets
item.description: Injective and BDACS will explore KRW1 settlement for tokenized assets, while issuance and redemption remain limited to approved institutions and regulatory clearance.

item.title: BaseSwap: How to Judge a Route for an Unfamiliar Pair
item.description: For an unfamiliar pair, BaseSwap’s quote is useful only after you check token identity, route depth, fees and minimum received against your trade size.

item.title: Three Checks for a Bridge Deposit Confirmation
item.description: A bridge status label does not prove a deposit is safe to credit; check source-chain inclusion, the exact deposit, and the destination transaction separately.

item.title: JPMorgan deploys its dollar deposit token on Ethereum
item.description: JPMorgan has deployed its dollar deposit token on Ethereum mainnet for institutional clients, extending JPM Coin beyond Base and widening onchain settlement options.

item.title: World ID targets banks as Zoom human checks go live
item.description: World introduced a World ID package for financial firms and made its Zoom human check generally available, extending its proof system into institutional workflows.

item.title: Deutsche Bank puts crypto custody launch weeks away
item.description: Deutsche Bank says bitcoin and ether custody will launch in Germany within weeks, with stablecoin services to follow and Asian financial centres targeted next year.

item.title: Standard Chartered opens UAE crypto trading to wealth clients
item.description: Standard Chartered says eligible UAE Professional Investors can buy and sell Bitcoin and Ether through bank accounts, with custody and settlement inside its system.

item.title: Ledger reviews reseller controls after wallet implant theft
item.description: Ledger is reviewing sales and anti-tampering controls after attackers reportedly stole about $90 million by implanting components in reseller-sold wallets.

item.title: When a Replaced Transaction Breaks a Bridge Quote
item.description: On EVM chains, replacing a pending source transaction changes which call can execute at a nonce; bridge tracking and quote deadlines determine whether the transfer proceeds.

item.title: How to Fund a Node on One Chain From Another
item.description: Funding from another chain requires a payment path to the chain that charges the cost; a stablecoin balance elsewhere cannot pay native gas by itself.

item.title: Where Funds Go After a Cross-Chain Swap Fails
item.description: A failed cross-chain swap can leave funds on the source chain, in bridge escrow or on the destination chain; trace each transaction before retrying or claiming them.

item.title: Judge keeps Gemini’s $5 million CFTC order in force
item.description: A Manhattan judge denied the CFTC and Gemini’s bid to undo their 2025 consent order, leaving the paid $5 million penalty and injunction in force.

item.title: Why a Shorter Cross-Chain Swap Route Can Cost More
item.description: A cross-chain route with fewer hops can still return less: pool depth, price impact, destination gas and failure handling determine the net amount delivered.

item.title: What Bridge-and-Swap Does on Mantle
item.description: A Mantle bridge-and-swap routes an asset across chains, then trades it into a destination token; the bridge, swap, fees and failure points remain distinct.

item.title: How a Token With No Gas Can Fund Its Own Swap
item.description: An ERC-20 balance cannot pay its own first transaction fee; a compatible paymaster or funded relayer can front native gas and recover the cost in tokens.

item.title: Why Destination Events Can Precede Swap Status Updates
item.description: A destination-chain event can appear before a swap tracker changes status because receipts, relayers, indexers and finality checks run on separate timelines.

item.title: How to Fund a Solana Lending Market From Ethereum
item.description: Funding a Solana lending market from Ethereum takes two separate steps: bridge an accepted token to Solana, then deposit it through the market’s program.

item.title: What a cross-chain swap quote actually promises
item.description: A cross-chain quote estimates what reaches your destination wallet after routing, bridge costs and swaps; its output, fees and execution rules matter more than the headline rate.

item.title: Estimate Crypto Bridge Transfer Time by Stage
item.description: A bridge transfer has no single clock: estimate each chain’s confirmation, proof, relay and destination-finality stages, then track the stage that controls release.

item.title: What Counts as Proof of a Cross-Chain Transfer?
item.description: A useful cross-chain support ticket pairs the source receipt with the bridge message and destination execution, because one hash rarely proves delivery.
